summary.text: Andrew Ferguson has cautioned against knee-jerk or “sledgehammer” regulation of AI, saying regulators should not assume the worst outcomes and should proceed with caution. He has also said enforcers should intervene where AI is used to injure consumers or workers and should address firms that use dominance in an AI input to suppress innovation, using existing law-enforcement tools. In 2024, Ferguson stated that Congress had not given the FTC power to regulate AI standing alone and warned against stretching consumer-protection authority to regulate AI as such.

statements.text: I fear that a knee-jerk regulatory response will only squelch innovation, further entrench Big Tech incumbents, and perhaps even ensure that AI innovators move to jurisdictions that are friendlier to them

statements.text: This word of caution is not, however, a call to idleness. Where we see AI abused to injure consumers and workers, we should intervene.

attribution.speaker: Andrew Ferguson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The last thing we want is for a firm to gain dominance in an AI input and use that dominance to suppress or slow AI innovation.

attribution.speaker: Andrew Ferguson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: In sum, I encourage all of us to adopt a posture of regulatory optimism toward AI. Let us not assume the worst outcomes and rush to regulate on that basis.

attribution.speaker: Andrew Ferguson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: If antitrust enforcers race into the fray too quickly instead of giving the market time to develop, the markets may overtake our intervention and render it meaningless.

attribution.speaker: Andrew Ferguson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Congress has not given us power to regulate AI standing alone. We should not succumb to the panicked calls for the Commission to act as the country’s comprehensive AI regulator.

attribution.speaker: Andrew Ferguson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Businesses that exploit media hype and consumer unfamiliarity with this new technology to cheat people out of their hard-earned money should expect a knock on the door from the Commission and other law-enforcement agencies.

attribution.speaker: Andrew Ferguson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: I fear that if we confront AI with the regulatory sledgehammer, we will break it and deny to our citizens its potential promise. Instead, we must proceed with caution. We ought not to assume the worst possible outcomes from this new technology and regulate on that basis.

attribution.speaker: Andrew Ferguson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Kids today have AI doing their homework for them. We had Pokemon kids today have AI chatbots and Pokemon, so I guess not everything changes, but policymakers, advocates and parents would be foolish to think that the solutions of the past are sufficient for the problems of today.

attribution.speaker: Andrew Ferguson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Of course, we must be prudent in the steps we take to protect children online. As I've said in other contexts, our nation's tradition of light regulation compared to Europe is a huge part of what makes America the world's leader in technological innovation, particularly in the artificial intelligence race against China.

attribution.speaker: Andrew Ferguson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: This new law criminalizes sharing non-consensual intimate images including AI-generated deepfakes and requires platforms to remove such content within 48 hours of receiving a victim's request to do so.

attribution.speaker: Andrew Ferguson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: And we can do this while ensuring that America remains the world's beacon of innovation and that we win the AI race against our foreign rivals.

attribution.speaker: Andrew Ferguson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Instead, we must proceed with caution. Of course, technological innovation should promote the flourishing of citizens and their families, and we certainly should not be willing to permit harms to our citizens in pursuit of greater technological innovation. But we should not assume the worst possible outcomes of this new technology and regulate on that basis. Instead, as competition enforcers, we should use our trusted law-enforcement tools and watch carefully the development of this new technology.

attribution.speaker: Andrew Ferguson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: I write separately to ensure that no one confuses what we are doing today—holding generative-AI companies to the same standards for honest -business conduct that apply to every industry—with the regulation of AI qua AI.

attribution.speaker: Andrew Ferguson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: We may reach some AI-related activity incidental to enforcing those prohibitions, as we do today. But Congress has not given us power to regulate AI standing alone.

statements.text: Recent revelations about the state of the AI race means that now is a decisive moment for all of us.

attribution.speaker: Andrew Ferguson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Instead of chiding, I urge all of us to apply the lessons we have learned from overregulation to the most important question we confront as competition enforcers: what to do about artificial intelligence.
